history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration closely monitor the ongoing recruitment process of resident coordinators to ensure that the posts of resident coordinator and the key posts at resident coordinator offices are filled in an expeditious manner.
history.administration_response: By the end of 2021, 91 per cent of posts in the resident coordinator offices had been filled. The Development Coordination Office closely monitors the recruitment process to ensure that all posts are filled within the 120-day recruitment target, taking into consideration gender parity and equitable geographical representation. Considering the current vacancy rate of 9 per cent, which is normal in line with the overall vacancy rate across the United Nations Secretariat, the Board is requested to consider closing this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that 21 resident coordinator posts were still vacant as at 31 December 2021, while 20 resident coordinators ad interim were on board, and that the new administrative instruction on resident coordinator selection (ST/AI/2022/1) was promulgated in April 2022, the Board is of the view that further actions should be taken to fill the remaining vacant resident coordinator posts with long-term resident coordinators, while monitoring the implementation of the new administrative instruction. Therefore, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office is continuing to closely monitor recruitment processes and to ensure that vacant posts are filled in an expeditious manner. As at 31 March 2023, 110 resident coordinator positions were encumbered (85 per cent), with 20 positions vacant (15 per cent). This vacancy rate is in line with vacancy rates in the Secretariat and other United Nations entities. Of the 20 vacant positions, recruitment for 7 positions (5 per cent) has been completed; for 3 of these positions the new resident coordinators are expected to deploy shortly, and Government clearance is still pending for the remaining 4. The recruitment for the 13 remaining positions (10 per cent) is ongoing or will be launched imminently. While recruitments are expected to be complete by July 2023, it is expected that new vacancies will arise in the meantime due to the natural turnover of staff. Considering that ST/AI/2022/1 became effective in April 2022 and recruitment is ongoing under the new procedure, the Board is requested to consider the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that there were still 17 resident coordinator positions vacant as at 31 December 2022, and that some of them have long been vacant, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 521 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration closely monitor the ongoing recruitment process of resident coordinators to ensure that the posts of resident coordinator and the key posts at resident coordinator offices are filled in an expeditious manner.
history.reference_raw: Report of the Board for the year ended 31 December 2020 7
history.sg_progress: The Development Coordination Office is continuing to closely monitor recruitment processes and to ensure that vacant posts are filled in an expeditious manner, including by deploying resident coordinators ad interim while the recruitment processes are being completed. As at 1 August 2023, 107 (82 per cent) of resident coordinator positions were encumbered, with 23 (18 per cent) positions vacant. Out of the 23 vacant positions, recruitment for 14 positions has been completed, for 7 of which the new resident coordinators are expected to deploy imminently and for 7 of which government clearances remain pending. Recruitment for the nine remaining positions is ongoing or will be launched imminently. By the time these positions are filled, however, new vacancies are expected to arise. Vacant resident coordinator positions are a recurrent but transitory phenomenon. While premature departures by resident coordinators cannot be anticipated, the Development Coordination Office tries to minimize the number of vacancies through the arrangement to assign resident coordinators ad interim and an expedited recruitment process ensuring selection of suitable candidates. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration closely monitor the ongoing recruitment process of resident coordinators to ensure that the posts of resident coordinator and the key posts at resident coordinator offices are filled in an expeditious manner.
history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office is continuing to closely monitor the ongoing recruitment processes for resident coordinator posts and key positions in resident coordinator offices to ensure that resident coordinators are recruited expeditiously. As at 6 November 2024, 119 resident coordinator positions were encumbered (92 per cent), 1 was vacant and 10 were covered by a resident coordinator ad interim (8 per cent), the lowest share since the reform and well below the average vacancy rate in United Nations system agencies. Among the 10 resident coordinator positions covered by a resident coordinator ad interim, 5 are pending government clearance, 3 are under recruitment and the remaining 2 will be placed under recruitment imminently. In terms of key positions in the resident coordinator offices, the Development Coordination Office is at 85 per cent capacity, with 4 per cent of vacancies paused as part of strategic vacancy management and another 4 per cent of positions under recruitment. The Development Coordination Office therefore requests that this recommendation be closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the recommendation has been reiterated in A/79/5 (Vol. I), the Board considers the recommendation to be overtaken by events.
